🌌 About Our Team & Vision

Hi everyone! We are a driven team of software enthusiasts and builders who are deeply passionate about space science, embedded electronics, and application development. We love taking complex mathematical formulas and scientific principles and translating them into real-world software engineering solutions.

Our core team brings together a diverse mix of skills:

Project Architecture & Strategy: Leading the core logic, hardware design, and scientific baseline parameters.

Development & Collaboration: Working hard to build out our interface systems, manage our open-source code workflows, and refine our data tools.

Our collective project is NULLG, an advanced planetary site-scouting system designed to map hyper-arid deserts, polar impact craters, and volcanic lava tubes on Earth as high-fidelity terrestrial analogs for future lunar and Martian base layouts. We have already built a fully functional web application prototype using AI automation tools, featuring real-time environmental trait filters, data dashboards, and automated mission evaluation analytics.

🚀 Why You Should Join NULLG

Working Product Day 1: We don't just have an idea—we already have a live, clickable web application framework up and running.

Strong Science Focus: We are deeply analyzing real NASA flight data and planet surface telemetry (like the Atacama Desert and Haughton Crater metrics) to map exact geological similarities.

🛠️ Skills We Are Looking For

We are looking to expand our crew even further! If you have experience or interest in any of the following fields, we want you on our team:

UI/UX Designers / Creative Artists: To help refine our dark-themed mission control interface layouts, add gorgeous icons, and polish our presentation slides.

Data Researchers / Storytellers: To dig into open-source NASA Planetary Data System logs, find new Earth locations (caves, cold deserts, volcanic fields), and write compelling pitch descriptions.

Frontend Developers: To jump into our web application workspace and help customize interactive charts, add live maps, or link up analytical APIs.

Let’s build the next generation of interplanetary exploration tools together. Drop a message to join NULLG today!
summary:
We developed NULLG (NULL Spacecraft Fire Safety Intelligence), a specialized microgravity combustion simulator and telemetry dashboard designed to model how fire behaves in zero-gravity environments.
In space, the absence of buoyant convection turns flames into silent, nearly invisible blue spheres that burn slowly and trap toxic gases. Traditional Earth-based fire sensors and extinguishers fail under these conditions. NULLG addresses this challenge by enabling users to simulate and analyze space-cabin fire dynamics through customizable atmospheric inputs (O₂, CO₂, N₂, and pressure), zero-gravity polymer specimen testing parameters, ventilation airflow tracking, and AI-assisted hazard alerts. It also compiles structural flame-state metrics into clean data exports.
This project is critical because fire is one of the deadliest emergencies aboard a spacecraft. By helping researchers and crews predict how flames ignite, spread, and self-suffocate under varying cabin atmospheres and ventilation speeds, NULLG improves fire detection strategies and safeguards astronaut survival on long-duration space missions.

details:
We developed NULLG (NULL Spacecraft Fire Safety Intelligence), an interactive microgravity combustion simulator and safety telemetry dashboard. Unlike fires on Earth that flicker upward due to buoyant convection, flames in zero gravity form dim, nearly invisible blue spheres fueled purely by slow molecular diffusion.

NULLG models these complex microgravity fire dynamics in real time. Users can adjust critical spacecraft cabin parameters—including O₂, CO₂, and N₂ concentrations, cabin pressure, ventilation airflow speeds, and polymer material specimens. The system processes these inputs using microgravity combustion logic and an integrated AI engine to predict flame spread, burn rates, self-suffocation thresholds, and toxic gas buildup, exporting the results as structured telemetry reports.

Key Benefits

  • Safe Risk-Free Testing: Allows researchers, engineers, and students to test volatile spacecraft cabin atmospheres without the massive cost or danger of physical orbital experiments.
  • Instant Hazard Prediction: Alerts users to invisible fire risks, oxygen depletion zones, and dangerous ventilation conditions before ignition occurs.
  • Actionable Data Exports: Compiles simulation runs into clean, structured telemetry files for easy comparison and mission safety planning.

Intended Impact

Our goal is to make space exploration safer for astronauts on long-duration missions to the Moon, Mars, and orbital stations. Because Earth-style smoke detectors and fire extinguishers often fail in microgravity, NULLG helps spacecraft designers and mission planners understand how cabin airflow and gas mixtures influence fire behavior. By improving how crews detect and suppress spherical blue flames, our project directly supports astronaut survival and spacecraft resilience.

Tools, Software & Hardware Used

  • Development & AI Tools: We utilized Python for simulation logic and data processing, alongside Google AI / Gemini API for predictive hazard modeling and intelligent safety alerts.
  • Design & Presentation: We used AI visual generation tools and graphic editors to design our custom 4K metallic NULLG emblem and dark-mode terminal UI, and python-pptx for building our pitch deck.
  • Hardware: The platform was developed, tested, and rendered on a high-performance Windows workstation powered by an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 GPU (8GB VRAM), 32GB of RAM, and a 4TB NVMe SSD to ensure smooth visual rendering and responsive simulation performance.

Creativity & Innovation

Rather than presenting microgravity fire science as a static textbook chart, we designed NULLG to feel like a real-time spacecraft command terminal. We combined a high-contrast, dark-mode sci-fi interface—tailored for low-light space station environments—with interactive atmospheric dials and AI-driven hazard forecasting. Turning complex fluid and combustion physics into an intuitive, game-like simulation bridges the gap between advanced aerospace research and accessible educational design.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Physics Accuracy: We accounted for the complete absence of natural buoyant convection, focusing instead on molecular diffusion and forced cabin ventilation.
  • Human Factors & Visibility: Because zero-gravity flames emit faint blue light and trap carbon dioxide around sleeping crew members, we prioritized early detection metrics and toxicity warnings.
  • Usability Under Stress: We designed a high-contrast, clutter-free dark interface so operators can read critical oxygen and pressure alerts at a glance without eye strain.
